# `Tea.Cli.Ui`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Tea.Cli.Ui — the Cli shape's line-oriented view surface.

A `Lines msg` value is a structured, line-scoped view: a stack of styled
text lines. It is distinct from both the web `Element msg` and the Tui
`Screen msg`, so putting a web builder or a 2D cell-grid builder into a
`Lines` view is a compile-time type error (IPE-T0001), never a silent drop.

The builders take this module's OWN `Attribute msg`, interned `CliAttr`,
which exposes only honestly line-scoped styles: bold, underline, dim,
reverse, and terminal-palette foreground/background colour. There is no
2D geometry here — no cell spacing, no padding-in-cells, no vertical or
grid alignment — because a line-oriented surface cannot honour them; those
attributes are simply absent from the type rather than quietly discarded.

`text` is the plain-string escape hatch: `Cli.Ui.text s` renders `s` as one
line. `Cli.app`'s `view` field currently still returns `String`; migrating
that field to `Lines msg` (with `text` as the bridge for existing
string-returning views) is a tracked follow-up. This module ships the
structured surface and its shape-gate today.

## `none`

```ipe
none : Lines msg
```

An empty view — renders nothing.

## `text`

```ipe
text : String -> Lines msg
```

`text str` — render `str` verbatim as a single line, no styling.

## `line`

```ipe
line : List (Attribute msg) -> String -> Lines msg
```

`line attrs str` — one styled line: `str` under the line-scoped `attrs`.

## `lines`

```ipe
lines : List (Lines msg) -> Lines msg
```

`lines children` — stack `children` vertically, one under the next.

## `bold`

```ipe
bold : Attribute msg
```

Render a line's text in bold.

## `underline`

```ipe
underline : Attribute msg
```

Render a line's text underlined.

## `dim`

```ipe
dim : Attribute msg
```

Render a line's text dim (faint).

## `reverse`

```ipe
reverse : Attribute msg
```

Render a line's text in reverse video (swap foreground and background).

## `color`

```ipe
color : Color -> Attribute msg
```

`color c` — the foreground (text) colour, from the terminal palette.

## `bg`

```ipe
bg : Color -> Attribute msg
```

`bg c` — the background colour, from the terminal palette.
